excerpts.text: **Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers** (**ESCAPADE**) is a spacecraft mission to [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars "Mars") consisting of two spacecraft known as ***Blue*** and ***Gold***, which launched in November 2025.[[5]](#cite_note-berkeley1-5)[[4]](#cite_note-nssdc1-4)[[6]](#cite_note-Space.com1-6) The twin spacecraft will study Mars' [magnetosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetosphere "Magnetosphere") and how [solar wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_wind "Solar wind") contributed to the loss of most of the planet's [atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Mars "Atmosphere of Mars") over [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") history. In addition to its scientific goals, the mission is designed to demonstrate low-cost planetary space exploration. The mission is led by [UC Berkeley's Space Sciences Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Sciences_Laboratory "Space Sciences Laboratory") with Dr. Robert Lillis as Principal Investigator. It is part of [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")'s [SIMPLEx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_Innovative_Missions_for_Planetary_Exploration "Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration") program.[[7]](#cite_note-sn-20230413-7)[[8]](#cite_note-sn-20240425-8)

The spacecraft launched on November 13, 2025, from [Launch Complex 36A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Canaveral_Launch_Complex_36 "Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36") at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida.
